result: In 214 ME/CFS vs 189 controls across six clinics (90% met peak-effort criteria), ME/CFS had lower ventilation, breathing frequency, HR and ventilatory efficiency and more chronotropic incompetence across 20-100% peak VO2, with higher ventilatory equivalents and RPE, including in 99 pairs matched for peak VO2.
reason: Large multi-site CPET with chronotropic incompetence and effort criteria; adds submaximal-intensity and fitness-matched profile to the peak VO2/CI finding.

result: In 99 ME/CFS vs 99 controls matched for age and peak VO2 (~1 ml/kg/min), ME/CFS still showed inefficient exercise ventilation and higher perceived exertion during ramp cycling.
reason: Aerobic-capacity-matched design, the same approach the finding relies on; abnormalities persisted after fitness matching.

result: Among 85 adults with long COVID, 66% reported OI on active stand but POTS was found in only 2%; 26% had initial and 6% classical orthostatic hypotension, neither associated with OI, and OI was predicted only by higher HR at the SBP nadir (88 vs 75 bpm, OR 1.09).
reason: Long COVID population; the long COVID objective-autonomic finding (abnormalities including POTS in most) is the better target, and a 2% POTS rate runs against it; the ME/CFS POTS-prevalence finding is only secondary.

result: Among 85 adults with long COVID, POTS was found in 2% despite OI symptoms in 66% on active stand.
reason: The finding's core claim (cerebral hypoperfusion/preload failure in ME/CFS) was not measured; the POTS rate is covered by the neuro-lc-autonomic-objective retarget on the paired line.

result: In a prospective college cohort (4,501 students, 238 IM), students with severe baseline GI symptoms, low pre-illness IL-13 and/or IL-5 and severe GI symptoms during IM had a nearly 80% chance of severe ME/CFS 6 months later.

Among 106 students followed from before IM, low pre-illness IL-13/IL-5 plus severe GI symptoms at baseline and during IM gave a nearly 80% chance of severe ME/CFS at 6 months (18 severe, 30 ME/CFS, 58 recovered).
reason: Measures prospective pre-infection and acute predictors of post-infective illness, not cross-sectional cytokine levels against severity in established ME/CFS as Montoya did; fits the post-infective predictor finding.

result: On a 10-min passive lean test with capnography in 63 CFS patients (no controls), 60.3% had an abnormality at some visit (51%, 50%, 45% at visits 1-3), hypocapnia more common and more persistent than orthostatic tachycardia.
reason: Same test but does not report the HR/narrow pulse-pressure pattern the finding claims; adds repeat-visit yield and capnography, uncontrolled, so extends rather than replicates.

result: Resting or lean-induced hypocapnia (ETCO2 <=32 mmHg) was the most frequent and most persistent abnormality in 63 CFS patients tested up to 3 times, unrelated to anxiety scores.
reason: Independent cohort measuring orthostatic ETCO2 with capnography, same direction; uncontrolled and no CBF measure.

result: Meta-analysis of studies from 1988-2019 found deficits in visuospatial immediate memory (g=-0.55), reading speed (g=-0.82) and graphomotor speed (g=-0.59), plus episodic verbal/visual memory and attention, with executive and instrumental functions largely preserved.
reason: Independent meta-analysis with the same domains (speed, attention, memory impaired; higher functions spared); slight difference on working memory/executive.

result: In 113 mostly male, physically active military personnel ~159 days post COVID, hospitalised (n=35) and community-symptomatic (n=34) groups performed worse on submaximal and maximal exercise testing than controls, while community-recovered participants did not differ from controls.
reason: Same measure and direction in an independent LC cohort; small, preprint, peak VO2 numbers not given, and groups differed in age and BMI.
